title: Online shop
description: Customers, products, orders and the items in each order.
schema: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, city TEXT NOT NULL, joined_on TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), ordered_on TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE order_items (order_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(id), product_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES products(id), qty INTEGER NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (order_id, product_id));
seed: INSERT INTO products VALUES (1,'Notebook','stationery',50),(2,'Pen','stationery',10),(3,'Backpack','bags',800),(4,'Headphones','electronics',1500),(5,'Keyboard','electronics',1200),(6,'Water Bottle','misc',300),(7,'Desk Lamp','electronics',700);

problems.title: Cheap products
problems.statement: Return the `name` of every product that costs **less than 100**.
problems.expected: SELECT name FROM products WHERE price < 100
problems.note: The simplest shape: one table, one condition.

problems.title: Customers per city
problems.statement: Count the customers in each city. Return `city` and `customers`, the city with the most customers first, ties in alphabetical order of city.
problems.expected: SELECT city, COUNT(*) AS customers FROM customers GROUP BY city ORDER BY customers DESC, city
problems.hint: GROUP BY city, then ORDER BY the count and the city.
problems.note: You can ORDER BY an alias defined in the SELECT list.

problems.title: Customers who never ordered
problems.statement: Which customers have **never placed an order**? Return their `name`.
problems.expected: SELECT c.name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.id IS NULL
problems.hint: LEFT JOIN orders and keep the rows where the order is NULL.
problems.note: NOT EXISTS gives the same answer and reads closer to the question.

problems.title: Products nobody bought
problems.statement: Return the `name` of products that appear in **no order at all**.
problems.expected: SELECT p.name FROM products p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items i WHERE i.product_id = p.id)
problems.hint: NOT EXISTS with a subquery on order_items, or a LEFT JOIN with IS NULL.
problems.note: NOT EXISTS is safe with NULLs, unlike NOT IN over a nullable column.

problems.title: Delivered order totals
problems.statement: For every **delivered** order return `order_id` and its `total`, the sum of quantity times price of its items.
problems.expected: SELECT o.id AS order_id, SUM(i.qty * p.price) AS total FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY o.id
problems.hint: Join orders, order_items and products; multiply qty by price inside SUM.
problems.note: Filter the status in WHERE before grouping.

problems.title: Revenue by category
problems.statement: Using **delivered** orders only, return each product `category` and its `revenue`, largest revenue first.
problems.expected: SELECT p.category, SUM(i.qty * p.price) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY revenue DESC
problems.hint: Same joins as the order totals, grouped by category instead.
problems.note: The grain of the join is one row per order line, so SUM(qty * price) adds up correctly.

problems.title: Best customer
problems.statement: Which customer spent the most on **delivered** orders? Return their `name` and `total_spent`.
problems.expected: SELECT c.name, SUM(i.qty * p.price) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY c.id, c.name ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 1
problems.hint: Total per customer, order by it descending, take one row.
problems.note: LIMIT 1 hides ties. If ties matter, compare against MAX of the totals in a subquery instead.

problems.title: Running revenue
problems.statement: For **delivered** orders in date order, return `order_id`, the order's `total` and `running_total`, the revenue so far including this order. Order by date.
problems.expected: WITH t AS (SELECT o.id AS order_id, o.ordered_on AS d, SUM(i.qty * p.price) AS total FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY o.id) SELECT order_id, total, SUM(total) OVER (ORDER BY d, order_id) AS running_total FROM t ORDER BY d, order_id
problems.hint: Compute order totals in a CTE, then SUM(total) OVER (ORDER BY date).
problems.note: A window SUM with ORDER BY and no frame is a running total from the first row to the current one.

problems.title: Orders per month
problems.statement: How many orders (any status) were placed each month? Return `month` as `YYYY-MM` and `orders`, oldest first.
problems.expected: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', ordered_on) AS month, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders GROUP BY month ORDER BY month
problems.note: Grouping on an expression is fine; the alias can be reused in GROUP BY and ORDER BY in SQLite.
